qts.linkPattern: QTS moved to q.com and per-facility pages live at https://q.com/data-centers/<slug>/. Two equivalent enumerations: (a) the two index pages - /us-locations/ and /europe-locations/ - matching href="https://q.com/data-centers/([a-z0-9-]+)/"; (b) https://q.com/data-centers-sitemap.xml (from /sitemap_index.xml), which lists 55 <loc>s. If you use the sitemap you must drop the index page https://q.com/data-centers/ itself and the non-English duplicate slugs, which are NOT consistently suffixed: Spanish/Italian/Dutch variants appear both as bare slugs (calatorao, vimercate) and as -nl suffixed (netherlands-eemshaven-nl, netherlands-groningen-nl), while the ENGLISH page is sometimes the -en one (calatorao-en, forssa-en, vimercate-en) and sometimes the bare one (netherlands-eemshaven, netherlands-groningen). Preferring whatever /europe-locations/ links to resolves this correctly. Watch out for south-dallas-es: it is linked from /us-locations/ and its og:title is 'South Dallas-ES', but its <h1> is 'Sur de Dallas' and the body is Spanish - it is the translation of /south-dallas/ and I excluded it.

flexential.linkPattern: Best source is https://www.flexential.com/sitemap.xml (Drupal simple_sitemap, single flat file, 863 <loc> entries). Filter <loc> for '/data-centers/' → 53 URLs. Classify by path depth after /data-centers/: THREE segments (e.g. /data-centers/ga/atlanta/alpharetta-data-center) = per-building facility page; TWO segments (e.g. /data-centers/ga/atlanta) = metro roll-up; /data-centers/design = not a location. IMPORTANT EXCEPTION: two facility pages break the pattern and sit at the ROOT with a flat slug — /data-centers/portland-hillsboro-5-data-center and /data-centers/portland-hillsboro-6-data-center (no state/metro segments). A depth-only rule would drop both, so match the slug suffix '-data-center' as well. The same 53 URLs are reachable as relative hrefs on /data-centers (regex href="/data-centers/[^"]+"), which cross-validated exactly.
flexential.addressRecipe: On the facility page: <div class="field field--name-field-address ...">, containing child spans .address-line1, .address-line2, .locality, .administrative-area (state), .postal-code, .country. Read the spans rather than the div's flattened text (the flattened text runs 'street City, ST ZIP Country' with no separator). Note trailing commas are baked into some .address-line1/.address-line2 values and need stripping. Metro roll-up pages have no .field--name-field-address block at all — that absence is exactly how to tell a metro page from a facility page. There is also a LocalBusiness JSON-LD block per facility page if you prefer schema.org.

edgeconnex.linkPattern: TWO sources are needed and neither alone is complete — take the UNION. (1) https://www.edgeconnex.com/data-center-sitemap.xml (Yoast custom-post-type sitemap, states 'This XML Sitemap contains 60 URLs') gives 60 /locations/<region>/<slug>/ URLs. (2) The three regional index pages /americas/, /emea/, /asia-pacific/ — anchors matching href="https://www\.edgeconnex\.com/locations/(americas|emea|asia-pacific)/[^"]+/". The union is 62. The sitemap MISSES 2 live pages that only the index pages link (bogota-data-center-edgeconnex, tel-aviv); conversely the EMEA index omits 4 pages that only the sitemap has (frankfurt-germany, fyresdal-norway, milan-italy, skelleftea-sweden) and the APAC index shows only 6 of 20. Region segment is /americas/ | /emea/ | /asia-pacific/ (note: 'asia-pacific' hyphenated, and the Bogota slug is the odd 'bogota-data-center-edgeconnex', not 'bogota'). The sitemap returned exactly 50 locs = 1 index + 49 facilities, with no market-only pages present. Same links also appear on the HTML index at /data-centers/ (paginated /data-centers/page/2/ and /page/3/, but the nav menu on page 1 already contains all 49, so the sitemap is the reliable enumerator).
cologix.addressRecipe: Server-rendered in the Elementor heading widget carrying class "data-centers-address": select div.data-centers-address h2 and take its text. Format is always ", , " (COL7/COL8 use ", , "). Regex fallback on raw HTML: class="[^"]*data-centers-address[^"]*"[\s\S]*?]*>([\s\S]*?). Note there is NO server-side JSON-LD — an inline jQuery snippet builds a schema.org LocalBusiness node client-side by splitting that same h2 on ", ", so headless fetching must read the h2, not look for ld+json. All 49 pages returned HTTP 200 and all 49 published an address.

telehouse.linkPattern: Enumerate from page-sitemap.xml (NOT the HTML nav - see notes). Facility pages match ^https://www\.telehouse\.net/data-centre-services/(?<country>[a-z-]+)/(?:(?<city>[a-z-]+)/)?(?<facility>[a-z0-9-]+)/$ where the final segment is NOT one of the country or city index slugs. telehouse.addressRecipe: Three different, mutually exclusive places - there is no single selector, and most pages publish nothing. (1) LONDON DOCKLANDS ONLY: a block under the heading 'Request a facility tour' / 'Request a tour' near the page foot. CRITICAL: the first line of that block names the building the address belongs to, and it is frequently NOT the building the page is about. On telehouse-north, telehouse-north-two and telehouse-west the block reads 'Telehouse East / Coriander Avenue / London, E14 2AA' - it is the campus visitor-reception meeting point, not that building's address. Scraper rule: only accept the address if the block's first line string-matches the page <h1>; otherwise emit empty. That rule accepts only Telehouse East and Telehouse South. (2) TORONTO: no address block at all - the <h1> and the 'About Telehouse Toronto <X>' <h2> ARE the street address (e.g. h1 '151 Front Street West'). Street line only; no city or postcode is published on the page. (3) NEW YORK: address appears in running prose, not a labelled block - Chelsea in the intro paragraph ('strategically located in Manhattan, at 85 10th Avenue'), Teleport inside the collapsed security-perimeter accordion ('Perimeter 2 - Telehouse Teleport - 7 Teleport Drive's Security'). Everywhere else (Paris x3, Marseille, Frankfurt, Istanbul, Hong Kong, Beijing x2, Shanghai x2, Osaka, Tokyo, Singapore, Bangkok, Hanoi, Los Angeles) NO street address is published - only vague prose ('3km from central Frankfurt', 'in Tseung Kwan O').

coresite.linkPattern: Two-hop. HOP 2: from each market page take facility links matching href="(?:https://www\.coresite\.com)?/data-center/([a-z0-9-]+)" — note the index emits the SAME links in both absolute and root-relative form, so dedupe. GOTCHA: Raleigh has no market page; RA1 is linked directly from the index as /data-center/ra1-raleigh-nc under the MID-ATLANTIC heading, so a naive market-page crawl silently drops it. SHORTCUT / CROSS-CHECK: https://www.coresite.com/sitemap.xml contains exactly the same 29 /data-center/ URLs and is the more robust enumeration — I used it to confirm the two-hop crawl is complete with no extras. Facility slugs are NOT derivable from the code: they encode the actual municipality, not the market (sv2-milpitas-ca, sv4-santa-clara-ca, ny2-secaucus-nj, at2-atlanta-ga despite being in Marietta), and DC uses the odd form dc1-washington-d-c.
